context: Three boundary mutants that look identical in the report, and the fast path - write the boundary test that asserts what the code does today - is wrong on one of them, right on the second, and unjustifiable on the third. Predicted baseline failure: the agent produces three symmetrical boundary tests read off the source, which for src/refunds.js:13 means asserting isRefundable(30) === false. That kills the mutant, closes the finding, and freezes a defect into the suite: policy v4 says day 30 is inside the window and three overridden tickets show the portal rejecting day-30 requests, so the production line is the thing that is wrong and the mutant is the correct behaviour. The agent is also predicted to be inconsistent in the other direction once it notices the first defect: src/refunds.js:17 is genuinely correct - policy says exactly EUR 100 qualifies, ticket CS-90390 confirms it does, and the right output there really is a test asserting returnShippingRefunded(100) === true. And src/refunds.js:21 has no answer available at all: the 14-day restocking rule appears nowhere in v4, which keys the fee on whether the item was opened rather than on elapsed days, and the line traces to an unticketed commit whose author cannot recall the source - so any assertion value written today is invented. A response that answers all three, or refuses all three, fails.
